extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies and plan developers (and owners/operators of affected EGUs); Tribal plan developers; EPA reviewers
extracted.subtask_short: state plans for EGU emission guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing state (and Tribal) plans under CAA section 111(d) to implement emission guidelines for existing fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs), including methodologies for presumptive standards, baseline calculations, compliance demonstrations, and required plan components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define acronyms on first use
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed and is finalizing editorial amendments to define acronyms the first time they are used in the regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial requirement to improve clarity; no substantive change to requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include SI equivalents for heat-input standards
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed and is finalizing adding International System of Units (SI) equivalent for owners/operators of stationary combustion turbines complying with a heat input-based standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide SI-equivalent units alongside existing units for clarity and usability by regulated entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct regulatory cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed and is finalizing correcting errors in the current 40 CFR part 60, subpart TTTT, regulatory text referring to part 63 instead of part 60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical corrections to ensure regulatory text cites the correct parts; editorial only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of electric sales for combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of stationary combustion turbines subject to the heat input-based standard must maintain records of electric sales to demonstrate that they did not sell electricity above the threshold that would trigger the output-based standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a practical matter, include explicit requirement that records of electric sales be maintained to demonstrate non-applicability of output-based standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update referenced test methods
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed and is finalizing updating the ANSI, ASME, and ASTM International (ASTM) test methods to include more recent versions of the test methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and sources should use the updated versions of ANSI/ASME/ASTM test methods referenced in the regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance flexibilities for EGUs sharing generator or stack
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed and is finalizing adding additional compliance flexibilities for EGUs either serving a common electric generator or using a common stack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text will include mechanisms permitting certain shared-configuration EGUs to use alternative compliance constructs; see redline/strikeout regulatory text in docket for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of large vs small modification (steam generating units)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large modification is a physical change, or change in the method of operation, that results in an increase in hourly CO2 emissions of more than 10 percent when compared to the source's highest hourly emissions in the previous 5 years; small modification results in increase ≤10 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large modifications trigger unit-specific emission limits under NSPS; small modifications are not covered by the NSPS modification standards and remain existing sources subject to CAA section 111(d) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER and standard for large modifications (coal-fired steam units)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is amending the BSER for large modifications for coal-fired steam generating units to mirror the BSER for long-term coal-fired units: the use of CCS with 90 percent capture; the degree of emission limitation associated with CCS with 90 percent capture is an 88.4 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard of performance for steam generating units that undertake large modifications after May 23, 2023, is a unit-specific emission limit determined by an 88.4 percent reduction in the unit's best historical annual CO2 emission rate (2002 to date of modification). Compliance with testing, monitoring, and reporting requirements follows 40 CFR part 60, subpart TTTT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of small modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the EPA has not promulgated a NSPS for small modifications, any existing steam generating unit that undertakes a change that increases its hourly CO2 emissions rate by 10 percent or less will continue to be treated as an existing source that is subject to the CAA section 111(d) requirements being finalized today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small modifications do not trigger the NSPS modification provisions; state plans and 111(d) processes apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plans must achieve equivalent emission reductions to EPA BSER/presumptive standards
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must achieve an equivalent level of emission reduction to the degree of emission limitation achievable through application of the BSER as determined by the EPA; the standards of performance that states establish must be no less stringent than the presumptive standards of performance in the applicable emission guidelines (after accounting for any application of RULOF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be 'satisfactory,' a state plan must address each affected EGU and achieve at least the level of emission reduction that would result from each affected EGU achieving its presumptive standard (accounting for any RULOF applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot count reductions from non-affected sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Emissions reductions from sources not affected by the final emission guidelines may not be counted towards compliance with either a source-specific or aggregate standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans may not rely on emission reductions at non-affected fossil fuel-fired EGUs or installation/operation of other electricity-generating resources not subject to these emission guidelines for demonstrating compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan required components for each affected EGU
rubrics_metrics.description: For each affected EGU within the state, the state plan must include a standard of performance and compliance schedule; coal-fired affected EGUs must have increments of progress and, if they plan to permanently cease operation and rely on such cessation, an enforceable commitment and reporting obligations and milestones; state plans must specify the test methods and procedure for determining compliance with the standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each individual unit must have a source-specific standard and schedule. For coal units relying on closure, commitments must be enforceable by the state (rule, order, permit, or other legal instrument) so they become federally- and citizen-enforceable upon EPA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of EPA presumptive methodology and subcategory assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: A state, when establishing standards of performance for affected EGUs in its plan, must identify each affected EGU and specify into which subcategory each affected EGU falls, then use the corresponding methodology for the given subcategory to establish the presumptively approvable standard of performance for each affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may deviate from the EPA methodology to adopt a more stringent standard without invoking RULOF. States may apply RULOF to justify a less stringent standard or longer compliance schedule for a particular affected EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline emission performance calculation (8-quarter rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish baseline emission performance for an affected EGU (except low-load NG/oil), a state will use the CO2 mass emissions and corresponding electricity generation data for any continuous 8-quarter period from 40 CFR part 75 reporting within the 5-year period immediately prior to the date the final rule is published in the Federal Register; for low-load natural gas- and oil-fired subcategories use CO2 mass emissions and corresponding heat input for a continuous 8-quarter period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate baseline as total CO2 mass (lbs) over the 8 quarters divided by total gross electricity generation (MWh) or total heat input (MMBtu) to obtain lbs CO2/MWh or lbs CO2/MMBtu. States should pick the most representative continuous 8-quarter period; EPA will generally defer to a state's reasonable exercise of discretion. The approach avoids sorting/filtering data and averages out short-term variability. If a state wishes to vary the baseline calculation in a way that results in a less stringent standard, it must use the RULOF mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance demonstration frequency and method
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing a requirement that compliance be demonstrated annually. For all subcategories except low-load NG/oil, compliance is based on lb CO2/MWh derived from total reported CO2 mass emissions divided by total reported electric generation during the compliance calendar year. For low-load NG/oil subcategory, compliance is based on lb CO2/MMBtu derived from total reported CO2 mass emissions divided by total reported heat input during the compliance calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance period is a calendar year; the compliance demonstration must occur by March 1 of the following year. Example: 2030 compliance period demonstration due by March 1, 2031.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-based vs mass-based standards and translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance must be established as either a rate or, for certain subcategories, a mass of emissions. If a state allows mass-based compliance it must first calculate the rate-based emission limitation that corresponds to the presumptive standard and then explain how it translated that rate-based emission limitation into the mass that constitutes an affected EGU's standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must document methodology and equivalency when using mass-based standards derived from rate-based presumptive standards; see section X.D for additional guidance on compliance flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategory definitions and fuel-status rule (Jan 1, 2030)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcategories are based on fuel type (coal-, natural gas-, or oil-fired) determined by the status of the source on January 1, 2030; natural gas- and oil-fired units are further subcategorized by load level (base, intermediate, low).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For units that retain the capability to fire coal after the final rule publication date, that fired any coal during the 5-year period prior to that date, or that will fire any coal after that date and before January 1, 2030, the plan must include a requirement to remove the capability to fire coal before January 1, 2030.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal subcategory enforceable cessation commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs in the medium-term coal-fired subcategory, states must include sources' enforceable commitments to cease operating before January 1, 2039, in their plans. The state plan must specify the calendar date by which the affected EGU plans to cease operation; the commitment must be enforceable by the state (rule, agreed order, permit, or other legal instrument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon EPA approval of the state plan, that commitment will become federally- and citizen-enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term coal presumptive standard (CCS 90% capture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term coal-fired EGUs have a BSER of CCS with 90 percent capture and a degree of emission limitation of 90 percent capture of the mass of CO2 in the flue gas and an 88.4 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross) on an annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish the presumptively approvable standard by calculating the unit-specific baseline emission performance and multiplying by 0.116 (the complement of 88.4%). Example: baseline 2,000 lbs CO2/MWh -> standard = 2,000 * 0.116 = 232 lbs CO2/MWh. Affected long-term coal EGUs must comply with federally enforceable increments of progress (see section X.C.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal presumptive standard (40% NG co-firing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medium-term coal-fired EGUs that commit to cease operation before January 1, 2039 have a BSER of 40 percent natural gas co-firing on a heat input basis, which translates to a 16 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh) compared to baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish the presumptively approvable standard by calculating the unit-specific baseline emission performance and multiplying by 0.84 (the complement of 16%).
